latest.title: CEO Succession
latest.content:
11 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 3266U
Vanquis Banking Group PLC
11 September 2026
This announcement contains inside information.
Ian McLaughlin to step down as Vanquis CEO
London - 11 September 2026 - Vanquis Banking Group plc ('the Group' or 'Vanquis') announces today that Ian McLaughlin has informed the Board of his intention to step down as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for personal reasons by no later than the end of the year.
John Natalizia, currently Deputy CEO and CEO of Snoop, will be appointed as Interim CEO when Ian steps down, subject to regulatory approval.
Over the next few months, John will attend Board meetings and Ian will work closely with him to ensure an orderly transition. In the meantime, the Board will initiate an internal and external executive search process to identify a successor to lead the Group.
John Natalizia joined Vanquis following the acquisition of the fintech uSnoop Limited ('Snoop') in July 2023 and has been a member of the Group Executive Committee since then. He was appointed Deputy CEO in April 2026 and currently has executive responsibility for the Group's product offerings, and technology and change delivery, which incorporates the Gateway transformation programme. He has over 25 years of banking experience, including a range of commercial, digital, operational and transformation roles at Virgin Money and MBNA, before establishing Snoop as a co-founder. During his time at Virgin Money and MBNA, John held senior roles in their respective credit card businesses, including responsibility for the build, migration and successful launch of Virgin Money's credit card business and the strategic transformation of MBNA's business.
Sir Peter Estlin, Group Chairman, commented:
"On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank Ian for his significant contribution to the turnaround of Vanquis, and the establishment of the strategy and business priorities for the Group's future success. Under Ian's leadership the Group has undertaken a significant transformation and returned to profitability with a much clearer pathway to delivering attractive and sustainable returns for shareholders.
Although there is still work to do, the Group is well placed to build on the progress Ian has led. The Board has confidence in the strategy and the management team under the leadership of John and Dave Watts, the Group's Chief Financial Officer."
Ian McLaughlin commented:
"I would like to thank the Board and all my colleagues for their hard work and support to deliver the operational and financial turnaround of the business. Significant progress has been made. The Group is now much better positioned to deliver on the trajectory we have set out for shareholders, and to continue with our purpose serving the customers who need us most. It has been a privilege to lead Vanquis through this phase, and I wish everyone involved continued success and happiness."

company_30s.what_they_do: Vanqius builds a cloud‑based banking platform that lets small businesses manage accounts, payments and cash flow through a single API. The service is aimed at merchants who want to replace legacy banking with a flexible, digital solution.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The global SME banking market is moving rapidly toward online‑only models. Vanqius offers a developer‑friendly platform that can be embedded in e‑commerce sites, accounting software and point‑of‑sale systems, giving it a clear path to capture a share of this growing niche.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a restructuring phase. A CEO transition and a new board composition have just been announced, and the firm is still reporting on a six‑month interim period. No revenue figures are publicly disclosed, and the share price is essentially a penny‑stock that has not traded recently.

rns_narrative: The latest filings show a leadership overhaul: the CEO is stepping down and a new executive is being installed. A director’s shareholding has been updated, and the board is tightening its voting structure. The company has also released interim results for the first half of the year, but no concrete profit numbers are available.

These events cluster around two themes: (1) governance realignment and (2) a pause to prepare for a potential earnings announcement. The tone of the filings suggests the company is trying to reassure investors that it has a plan for the future.
The lack of a clear catalyst in the filings means the market is still waiting for a signal that the new leadership will drive growth.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism around a new CEO
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Followers are praising the leadership change, saying the new executive could unlock the platform’s potential and bring in new partners.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Some skeptics worry that the company still has no proven revenue stream and that the leadership switch may be a last‑ditch attempt to keep the stock alive.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The conversation has remained steady and mildly bullish; no dramatic swings have been seen in the last week.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat, indicating no public search interest. This silence creates a window for surprise if a catalyst emerges.

near_term_catalysts: The formal announcement of the new CEO’s appointment and any accompanying strategic roadmap.
Release of the full year 2026 results, which could show a turnaround or at least a clearer financial picture.
Any partnership or integration announcement with a larger payment processor or ERP vendor.
A funding round that would provide fresh capital for product development and marketing.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that accompanies any of the above events, a sudden shift in the company’s messaging toward profitability, or a clear revenue number in the next earnings release.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a post‑capitulation recovery. If the new leadership delivers a concrete plan or a positive earnings surprise within the next three months, the mean‑reversion play could start. Until then, the market is still waiting for confirmation.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: A deep crash creates a huge upside if the company can turn the new leadership into a growth story. The mean‑reversion thesis is strong because the market has largely ignored the stock, leaving a large gap between current price and the level the platform could command if it gains traction. Historical data from similar deep‑crash setups shows that a 50% recovery from the low can still deliver a 150% return on the original price.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is that the company never produces a clear revenue stream or that the new CEO fails to deliver a turnaround. A continued lack of profitability could push the price back toward its current low. The worst‑case scenario is a further decline to a price that is essentially worthless for retail investors.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is several times the current price if the platform gains adoption; downside is limited to the present price because the stock is already near its lowest point.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a confirmed earnings release that shows a positive trend or after a partnership announcement. Size the position to risk only a small fraction of your portfolio (e.g., 1–2%) and set a stop just below the most recent low. Use a trailing stop to protect gains if the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a volume spike of at least 50% over the 20‑day average combined with a clear statement of a new revenue target or funding round. This would give the market a reason to buy.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no immediate delisting or bankruptcy risks identified.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Vanqius sits at a deep low with a fresh CEO and no obvious catalyst yet; if the new leadership can deliver a credible growth plan within the next three months, the upside is significant and the downside remains capped at the current price.
